paperMetadata.title: Towards Better Tool Use and Agent Systems: An Empirical Analysis

abstract: In recent years, large language models (LLMs) have demonstrated the potential to be augmented with external tools like code execution environments, calculators, search engines, and APIs. This paper explores the domain of tool use within autonomous agent frameworks, focusing on effective tool selection, action planning, and error recovery. By introducing a novel architecture, ToolManager, we aim to enhance the multi-step reasoning capabilities of LLMs. ToolManager employs a dynamic planning module that learns to select and sequence tools based on the task requirements, using a feedback loop for error correction. Our experiments show significant improvements in task completion rates and efficiency compared to state-of-the-art systems such as ReAct and Toolformer. The primary contributions of our work include the design of a tool selection strategy driven by reinforcement learning, the integration of a feedback mechanism for error recovery, and extensive evaluations across diverse scenarios. These contributions advance the understanding of autonomous tool use in agent systems, opening new avenues for research in this emerging field.

contributions.title: Dynamic Tool Selection Strategy
contributions.description: We propose a novel tool selection strategy using reinforcement learning to dynamically choose tools based on task requirements.
contributions.novelty: Unlike existing methods that rely on static tool selection, our approach adapts to the task context, optimizing tool use efficiency.

contributions.title: Feedback Mechanism for Error Recovery
contributions.description: A feedback loop mechanism is introduced to correct errors in tool use, enhancing the robustness of multi-step reasoning processes.
contributions.novelty: This mechanism allows the system to learn from its mistakes, which is not addressed by current autonomous agent frameworks.

contributions.title: Comprehensive Evaluation Framework
contributions.description: We provide a comprehensive evaluation framework to benchmark tool use in agent systems across various scenarios and metrics.
contributions.novelty: The framework offers standardized evaluation protocols, facilitating consistent comparisons with previous work.

methodology.problemFormulation: We aim to improve the efficiency and accuracy of tool use in autonomous agent systems by addressing tool selection, action planning, and error recovery.
methodology.approach: The ToolManager architecture combines reinforcement learning for tool selection and a feedback loop for error recovery, optimizing the execution of multi-step reasoning tasks.

components.name: Dynamic Planning Module
components.role: To select and sequence tools based on the task requirements.
components.details: Uses a policy network trained with reinforcement learning, receiving state representations of the task and available tools.

components.name: Feedback Loop
components.role: To correct errors in tool execution.
components.details: Monitors the output of each tool step, identifying discrepancies and triggering corrective actions.

assumptions: The agent has access to a predefined set of tools.
Tasks can be decomposed into identifiable steps that can be addressed by available tools.
limitations: The system's performance is dependent on the quality of the feedback signals.
Scalability may be constrained by the computational overhead of maintaining dynamic tool selection.

evidence.description: Validation of tool selection efficiency and error recovery effectiveness.

setup.context: Tasks requiring multi-step reasoning, including mathematical problem solving and data retrieval.

evaluation.protocol: Compare ToolManager against ReAct and Toolformer under controlled conditions.

evidence.analysis: ToolManager outperformed baselines in both accuracy and efficiency, validating the effectiveness of dynamic tool selection and feedback mechanisms.
